checks.s: The demand registration compromise clause specifies exactly two (2) demand registrations.
The demand registration clause states a minimum gross-proceeds or minimum aggregate offering amount threshold of at least $10,000,000.
The demand registration clause provides that failed, withdrawn, or not-declared-effective registrations do not count against the two-demand cap.
The demand registration eligibility trigger is set at approximately 4 years post-closing.
The demand registration eligibility trigger includes an alternative of 180 days post-Qualified IPO, whichever is earlier than the 4-year trigger.
The demand registration initiating-holder threshold is above 30.95% and at or below 38.10% of Registrable Securities, approximately 35%.

The rationale measures the initiating-holder threshold against all then-outstanding Registrable Securities and explains that Crestline's 2,666,667 shares (38.10% of 7,000,000) let it initiate alone while Pinehurst's 2,166,667 shares (30.95%) do not.
The demand registration clause gives the Company a deferral or postponement right capped at approximately 90 days.
The Company may exercise the demand registration deferral or postponement right no more than once per 12-month period.
The demand registration deferral or postponement right requires a good-faith board determination.
The S-3 or shelf registration compromise proposes a frequency of approximately 3 per 12-month period.
The S-3 or shelf registration minimum offering size is approximately $3,000,000, within the $2,000,000-to-$4,000,000 range.

The S-3 compromise rationale says that S-3 or shelf filings impose a lower administrative burden on the Company than full S-1 demand registrations and uses that distinction to justify a more permissive frequency.
The Major Investor threshold for information rights is between 250,000 and 500,000 shares, approximately 350,000 shares.
The rationale shows the dollar amount represented by the Major Investor threshold at the Series B price of $12.00 per share.
The rationale identifies which investors qualify or are excluded based on the capitalization table.
The information rights clause gives monthly management reports only to holders above a higher threshold, such as holders of at least 1,000,000 shares.
The information rights clause gives standard quarterly and annual deliverables to all Major Investors at the lower threshold of approximately 350,000 shares.
The board observer rights threshold is between 250,000 and 1,000,000 shares, approximately 500,000 shares.
The board observer clause gives the Company a narrowly tailored right to exclude the observer for attorney-client privilege or competitive conflicts.
The pro rata rights clause covers priced equity rounds.
The pro rata rights clause covers convertible instruments above a specified threshold of approximately $5,000,000, within the $4,000,000-to-$6,000,000 range.
The pro rata rights clause excludes option pool increases from the definition of “New Securities.”
The pro rata rights clause requires a governance safeguard, such as board approval including at least one Series B director, for option pool increases or other sensitive carve-outs.
The compromise clause retains pay-to-play.
The pay-to-play provision requires an investor to participate for at least 50% of its pro rata share.
The pay-to-play penalty converts a non-participating investor's shares to shadow preferred stock rather than common stock.
The rationale explains why full conversion to common stock is disproportionate compared with conversion to shadow preferred stock.
The pay-to-play “Qualified Financing” trigger specifies a dollar threshold of at least $5,000,000.
The pay-to-play clause includes an exception for a down round, such as a financing priced below a specified percentage of the $12.00-per-share Series B OIP.
The shadow preferred conversion clause identifies anti-dilution adjustment as a stripped right.
The shadow preferred conversion clause identifies right of first offer or pro rata rights as a stripped right.
The shadow preferred conversion clause identifies board designation and observer rights as stripped rights.
The shadow preferred conversion clause specifies that the retained liquidation preference is 1x non-participating.
The shadow preferred conversion clause specifies that retained dividend rights are 8% non-cumulative.
The rationale explains that shadow preferred conversion is more balanced than full conversion to common because it strips governance and protective rights while retaining economic preferences.
The MFN provision uses a notice-and-election mechanic rather than an automatic ratchet.
The MFN covers only an enumerated list of core economic rights, such as liquidation preference, dividends, anti-dilution, redemption, and registration rights.
The MFN provision expressly excludes governance rights, such as board seats, voting rights, and protective provisions.
The MFN sunset is approximately 48 months or upon a Qualified IPO, whichever is earlier.
The rationale explains how the approximately 48-month MFN sunset aligns with the expected 2028-2029 IPO window, including that May 2025 plus 48 months is May 2029.
The MFN provision excludes a down round, such as a future distressed financing priced below the $12.00-per-share Series B OIP.
The rationale explains the economic inequity of applying the MFN in down-round scenarios, where new investors accept distressed pricing risk that existing holders do not bear.
The MFN clause lets holders of a majority of outstanding Series B Preferred waive the MFN for a specific transaction.
The deliverable includes a concession map or summary table showing approximately how many points land closer to the Company, closer to investors, and at genuine midpoints or novel compromises.

The deliverable preserves or expressly notes compatibility with Pinehurst's existing Series A rights: 1 demand registration, 2 S-3/year, a 500,000-share Major Investor threshold, board observer rights as lead Series A investor, and pro rata rights on priced rounds, with no pay-to-play or MFN.

Every compromise clause with a share-based threshold, including the Major Investor, board observer, and monthly reporting thresholds, includes anti-dilution adjustment language for stock splits, stock dividends, combinations, recapitalizations, or similar events.
The pro rata rights clause includes an employee equity plan carve-out.
The pro rata rights clause includes a strategic acquisition carve-out.
The pro rata rights clause includes an equipment financing carve-out.
The pro rata rights clause includes an IPO issuance carve-out.
The deliverable provides contract-ready clause language for registration rights, including demand and S-3 rights.
The deliverable provides contract-ready clause language for information and observer rights.
The deliverable provides contract-ready clause language for pro rata and pay-to-play rights.
The deliverable provides contract-ready clause language for the MFN.
For each of the four provisions, the deliverable gives a negotiation rationale that identifies both parties' opening positions, explains the concession logic, and justifies the landing point.
The MFN “Subsequent Financing” trigger covers both equity securities and convertible instruments.
The pay-to-play clause lets a Non-Participating Investor regain Major Investor status by participating at a sufficient level in a later Qualified Financing.
The pay-to-play clause states that regaining Major Investor status does not reverse the investor's prior shadow preferred conversion.
The deliverable either proposes a compromise for dispute resolution between JAMS San Francisco and Delaware Court of Chancery or explicitly flags dispute resolution for separate negotiation.
The board observer rights clause explicitly states whether observers may attend committee meetings.
